question.text: The first <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> and second <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> ionization energies (kJ/mol) of a few elements designated by Roman numerals are given below. Which of these would be an alkali metal?

solution.text: As alkali metals have the lowest <math><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> values in their respectively periods and also there is a large jump between <math><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> due to the removal of second electron from the noble gas core, therefore, out of the given <math><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> values (II) belongs to alkali metals.
